status: AUDIT — recognition contract snapshot, not a taxonomy amendment

class.name: Protected Information Access Integrity
class.definition: The property by which information held or handled by an AI-mediated system or its dependent infrastructure remains accessible, obtainable, disclosable and modifiable only within an independently established authorisation boundary. The property concerns realised information protection, without requiring a particular access-control implementation or an authority inference by the system.
class.invariant: Protected information must remain within the independently established authorisation boundary for access, acquisition, disclosure and modification. Technical reachability, absent authentication or ineffective access restrictions must not permit an unauthorised information operation.

required_conditions: Identifiable information is held or handled by an AI-mediated system or its dependent infrastructure.
An independently evidenced confidentiality or integrity boundary restricts access, acquisition, disclosure or modification of that information for the actor, operation and context.

Occurrence evidence demonstrates that at least one such information operation crosses that boundary. A successful unauthorised retrieval or modification is sufficient; a theoretical route alone is not.
Identifiable information and its independently evidenced confidentiality or integrity boundary are established for an AI-mediated system or dependent infrastructure.
A concrete access, acquisition, disclosure or modification attempt or operation materially tests that boundary.
Observed response or verification shows that the unauthorised information operation is prevented or that the operation remains within its authorised information boundary.
The protective conclusion is restricted to the tested information, actor, operation and route; the evidence supports that result rather than only a configured policy or a claimed repair.

exclusions: Class scope exclusion (all results): The information is deliberately public for the assessed operation and no independent integrity or other access restriction governs that operation. Public readability does not authorise public modification.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The only material property is custody of authentication material. Assess Authentication Material Custody Integrity; separate private content or other protected information can independently engage this class.

Not aligned exclusion: The observed information operation is validly authorised within the independently established boundary. An approved test does not by itself authorise public release of protected information.

Not aligned exclusion: Only a hypothetical vulnerability, exposed endpoint, unverified capability claim or unsuccessful attempt is established, without demonstrated protected-information access, acquisition, disclosure or modification.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The issue is solely accuracy, availability, provenance, secondary-purpose permission or audit reconstruction, without an independently engaged information access or integrity boundary.

class.name: Authentication Material Custody Integrity
class.definition: The property by which credentials, bearer tokens, API secrets, private authentication keys and comparable secret material retain their independently established custody and protection boundary during storage, use, transmission, delegation, replacement and retirement. Exposure or acquisition outside that boundary is independently assessable before any later use to impersonate a principal or access a resource.
class.invariant: Authentication material must remain under authorised custody throughout its lifecycle. Its secret content must not become available to an unauthorised recipient or route, or undergo unauthorised custody-changing modification or replacement. Valid delegation and lifecycle transitions must preserve the applicable protection boundary.

required_conditions: Identifiable material serves an authentication or authorisation function, or contains the protected secret content needed to exercise that function, in an AI-mediated system or dependent infrastructure.
An independently evidenced custody boundary governs who or what may hold, receive, disclose, modify or replace the material in the assessed lifecycle stage.

Occurrence evidence demonstrates exposure outside that boundary, unauthorised acquisition, or unauthorised custody-changing modification or replacement. Demonstrated retrievability of protected secret content is sufficient without proof of subsequent credential use.
Authentication material, its AI-mediated system or dependent infrastructure, and the applicable authorised custody boundary are identified.
A concrete handling operation, delegation, lifecycle transition or exposure attempt materially tests custody protection.
Observed handling or verification shows that the secret remains confined to authorised holders, recipients and pathways, with the applicable protection preserved through the tested operation.

The finding is limited to the tested material, operation and stage. Absence of reported misuse, ordinary credential availability, a missing key or an unverified rotation claim does not supply this evidence.

exclusions: Class scope exclusion (all results): The material is only a non-secret identifier, public connection identifier, public verification key or public client configuration that is intended to be available in the assessed context. A separately exposed secret or unauthorised protected-information operation requires its own assessment.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The issue concerns only coherent propagation of expiry, revocation, refresh or replacement into sessions and dependent operations. Assess Authentication-State Continuity unless a separate custody property is evidenced.

Not aligned exclusion: Credential handling or delegation is validly authorised and preserves the applicable custody boundary. Mere credential possession or ordinary authorised use is not a custody defect.

Not aligned exclusion: Only a theoretical vulnerability, unverified secret classification, unusable placeholder or unsuccessful attempt is shown; protected authentication material is not demonstrated outside custody.
Not aligned exclusion: Material is already invalid and no residual secret-protection or custody obligation is independently established. Do not assume every expired token remains a usable secret.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The only property is the scope of an action performed using a credential, without a distinct custody issue. Assess the applicable authority or action class.

class.name: Epistemic Reliance Calibration
class.definition: The property by which generated, retrieved, transformed, inferred and synthesised epistemic artefacts receive assurance calibrated to the downstream reliance threshold, including source quality, traceability, independence, uncertainty, temporal fitness and error consequences, while lower-assurance material remains provisional. Fitness is assessed for the actual purpose and workflow stage for which the output is supplied, including drafting. Specificity, certainty and framing must remain proportionate to the supporting evidence and that purpose.
class.invariant: Before an epistemic artefact is promoted, accepted, or used in a materially consequential decision, its assurance posture must meet the downstream reliance threshold, calibrated to source quality, traceability, independence, uncertainty, temporal fitness, and error consequences. Lower-assurance material must remain provisional. Provisional status permits appropriately limited reliance. It does not excuse material inaccuracies that make an output unfit for the purpose for which it is supplied. Where evidence cannot support a detail, the output must generalise, qualify, omit that detail or seek verification without distorting material meaning.
exclusions: Class scope exclusion (all results): Purely fictional, creative, symbolic, role-play, expressive, or contemplative generation where empirical truth is not a task condition.

Not aligned exclusion: Exploratory brainstorming, hypothesis generation or modelling is clearly represented as provisional, remains fit for its bounded exploratory purpose, and is not subsequently relied upon as verified or decision-ready.
Not aligned exclusion: Approximation where approximation is explicitly compatible with the task and reliance condition.

Not aligned exclusion: Material is clearly marked unverified or low-confidence, remains fit for the bounded purpose for which it is supplied, and is not subsequently promoted into an unsupported higher-reliance state. Provisional status does not by itself excuse material inaccuracies that make the output unfit for that purpose.
Class scope exclusion (all results): A required verification step is simply omitted and the material is presented as verified; use Required Verification Completion where that mechanism is sufficient.

Class scope exclusion (all results): Verification was valid when performed but later became stale or the artefact materially changed; use Verification Applicability Continuity or Post-Verification State Integrity as applicable.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The issue is only source provenance, authorship, or lineage while the epistemic assurance of the content is otherwise adequate for the task.

required_conditions: A factual claim, citation, technical statement, calculation, interpretation, source representation, or comparable epistemic artefact is generated, retrieved, transformed, inferred, or synthesised.

The output has an evidenced intended purpose or downstream task for which factual accuracy, evidentiary fidelity, technical correctness, source integrity, traceability, uncertainty handling or equivalent epistemic assurance is materially consequential; identify the requirement for the actual workflow stage, including any drafting function.
The content accuracy, specificity, certainty, framing or assurance applied to the artefact is materially below the level required for that purpose and reliance condition.

The artefact is supplied, represented, propagated, incorporated, submitted or accepted as usable for the reliance-bearing purpose or workflow stage without its required accuracy or epistemic threshold being satisfied. Draft status or an expectation of later human review does not by itself establish fitness for that purpose.

The mismatch materially affects or creates a material risk to decision-making, evidentiary use, professional work, institutional process, public reliance, technical correctness, or another reliance-bearing outcome.
An epistemic artefact is proposed for reliance with material error consequences.

Content accuracy and assurance meet the requirement for the actual purpose and workflow stage. Specificity, certainty and framing remain proportionate to source quality, independence, traceability, uncertainty and temporal fitness, without distorting material meaning.

The output, supporting evidence and reliance decision demonstrate fitness for that bounded use and show that lower-assurance material remained restricted from unsupported higher reliance. A provisional label or an expectation of human review alone is insufficient.

class.name: Control Effectiveness Integrity
class.definition: The property by which an applicable, validly activated governance or protective control produces an effect sufficient and timely to prevent, contain, interrupt, redirect, mitigate or safely bound its governed hazard to the level required by its protective purpose and evidenced protection context. Heightened protection conditions require evidence; disability or neurodivergence alone does not establish incapacity.
class.invariant: When a protective control validly becomes operative, its effect must be timely, proportionate, and sufficient for the hazard and protection context it governs. Detection, warning, labelling, refusal language, escalation signalling, or other nominal activation is not by itself sufficient where the required protective effect is not achieved and the governed harmful state is delivered, continues, or remains inadequately contained. Required protective sufficiency may increase where evidenced developmental vulnerability, capacity limitation, temporary or situational consent impairment, acute distress, cognitive asymmetry, or comparable protection conditions materially affect the risk, but disability or neurodivergence alone must not be treated as incapacity.
exclusions: Class scope exclusion (all results): The applicable control does not become operative when a valid activation condition occurs; assess Required Control Activation.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The control becomes operative even though its valid activation or applicability conditions are not satisfied; assess Control Activation Validity.

Not aligned exclusion: The control becomes operative with a sufficient effect but its operative state is later lost, weakened, reset, or transformed before reaching the governed point; assess Control-State Preservation.

Class scope exclusion (all results): An operative governance signal fails to reach any capable endpoint or execution surface; assess the applicable governance-control reach class rather than treating non-delivery as inadequate control effect.
Not aligned exclusion: The control produces the protective effect required by its defined purpose and the remaining harm arises through an independent downstream mechanism.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The dispute is solely that policy should have required a stronger safeguard, without evidence of an applicable operational control or protective-effect obligation in the material context.

Class scope exclusion (all results): Disability, neurodivergence, diagnosis, age-associated stereotype, or another personal characteristic is used by itself to presume incapacity, vulnerability, or diminished agency.

required_conditions: A defined governance or protective control is applicable and validly becomes operative.

The control has an identifiable protective purpose requiring a material effect such as prevention, blocking, containment, interruption, redirection, limitation, escalation, mitigation, or another protection-compatible outcome.
The actual control effect materially falls short of that required protective purpose, allowing the governed hazard to be delivered, continue, escape containment, or remain insufficiently mitigated.

The shortfall is material in the evidenced hazard and protection context; where vulnerability, developmental status, capacity limitation, temporary or situational consent impairment, acute distress, cognitive asymmetry, or another heightened protection condition is relied on, that condition must itself be supported rather than presumed.
An applicable validly activated protective control faces its governed hazard.
The control produces a timely effect sufficient for its protective purpose and evidenced context, including any justified heightened protection.
Observed intervention and hazard outcome demonstrate the required containment or mitigation rather than activation alone.

class.name: Objective–Pathway Authority Separation
class.definition: The property by which each selected, continued, reconstructed or protected pathway toward an objective is independently assessed for applicable authority, consent, ethical admissibility, target, method, third-party rights, data custody and execution scope, including aggregate delegated and multi-step effects. Objective utility does not independently authorise the means.
class.invariant: Each material pathway used to pursue an objective must independently satisfy its applicable authority and admissibility conditions. Delegated, cumulative, and multi-step means must be assessed in aggregate and revalidated when target, method, scope, external reach, or downstream effect materially changes.
exclusions: Class scope exclusion (all results): A technically available capability is treated as permission without evidence that objective utility or task success materially drives the authority inference; use Capability-Authority Separation.

Class scope exclusion (all results): Authority validly established for one target, environment, principal, purpose, or scope is merely carried into another; use the applicable authority-transposition class unless objective-to-pathway dominance is independently evidenced.
Not aligned exclusion: A system explores alternative authorised means after a route becomes unavailable or prohibited and preserves all applicable authority and ethical constraints.
Class scope exclusion (all results): Persistence, planning, resource preservation, memory use, coordination, or task completion alone does not establish this class.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The event concerns deception, coercion, or manipulation of another decision-maker as the primary mechanism; classify the influence mechanism separately.

required_conditions: A system has a valid, purported, or operative objective, task, benchmark, evaluation goal, or delegated outcome to pursue.
A pathway materially advances, preserves, accelerates, or protects progress toward that objective.

The pathway is subject to an independent authority, consent, ethical-admissibility, target, method, third-party-rights, data-custody, or execution-scope constraint that is absent, narrower, unresolved, or adverse to the pathway.

Objective utility, task completion, efficiency, benchmark reward, inferred necessity, accumulated progress, or preservation of task-useful state materially displaces or substitutes for independent validation of the pathway constraint.
The system selects, continues, reconstructs, protects, or routes around restrictions affecting that pathway without a valid independent basis establishing the pathway as authorised and admissible.
An objective-directed process selects or continues a materially consequential pathway.
The actual means, including aggregate delegated effects, receive independent authority and admissibility assessment.
Pathway and authority evidence demonstrates the applicable consent, rights, custody and execution limits for the means actually used.

class.name: Actor–Action Attribution
class.definition: The property by which material actions and decisions remain reliably attributable to effective initiating and controlling actors, distinguishing human, model, agent, orchestrator, service, tool, policy, evaluator and infrastructure contributions, including transfers or shared control. Assess this property where material responsibility depends on distinguishing human direction, automated execution, agent-selected deviations or transfers of control. Preserved attribution can be Aligned even where the attributed conduct is harmful.
class.invariant: Each material action and decision record must identify the effective initiating and controlling actor or actors, distinguishing human, model, agent, orchestrator, service, tool, policy, evaluator, and infrastructure contributions and any transfer or sharing of control.
exclusions: Not aligned exclusion: The responsible actor is adequately attributable.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The issue is authorship provenance of content rather than operational responsibility for an action.
Not aligned exclusion: Multiple actors jointly contributed and the evidence accurately preserves the shared contribution.

required_conditions: A material action or decision is observable.
Attribution to the effective initiating or controlling actor is necessary for review or accountability.
Available evidence cannot reliably establish that attribution or collapses distinct actors into one undifferentiated source.
A material action involves initiating, controlling or shared actors.
Effective actor contributions and control transfers remain reliably distinguishable for that action.
Attribution evidence connects the action to its initiating and controlling actors and resolves relevant shared-control boundaries.

class.name: Service Availability and Degradation Integrity
class.definition: The property by which an AI-mediated service or material dependent function fulfils independently established availability and usable-functional-quality obligations. When service is materially interrupted, degraded, restricted or withdrawn, the responsible actor must meet the applicable continuity standard through proportionate operation, usable degraded service, timely recovery, feasible alternative or informed transition within its authority and control. Accurate outage reporting or a merely nominal fallback does not, by itself, establish that the required service continuity was preserved.
class.invariant: An AI-mediated service must maintain the usable availability and functional quality required by its independently established obligations. If material interruption, degradation, restriction or withdrawal occurs, the responsible actor must preserve the required function or provide proportionate, feasible and practically usable degraded operation, recovery, alternative access or transition in accordance with those obligations. Neither ordinary service variation nor adverse outcomes alone establish a breach; a service obligation, material functional shortfall and insufficient governed response must be evidenced.

required_conditions: A bounded AI-mediated service or material function has an independently established availability, usable-quality or continuity requirement applicable to the responsible actor, affected users or dependent workflow and relevant time; state the actual basis and threshold rather than inferring obligation from harm or popularity.

The service or function materially becomes unavailable, is withdrawn or restricted, or degrades in capability, latency, reliability, completeness, accessibility or another governed functional dimension, relative to the established applicable requirement.

The requirement calls for a specified degree of maintained usable function, timely recovery, safe degraded mode, feasible fallback or proportionate planned-change/termination response under the evidenced operating conditions.

The actor's actual availability, recovery, degraded operation, fallback or transition materially fails that applicable requirement; identify the specific omitted or ineffective measure or the breached availability threshold and what evidence establishes it.

The shortfall materially impairs the governed service use or dependent function. A later resolution does not retroactively demonstrate that availability or required transition held at the original decision time.

An AI-mediated service or material function has an independently established applicable availability or continuity obligation that is actually engaged by a service disruption, degradation, capacity pressure, material change or continuity transition.

The actor maintains the required usable function or activates a timely, proportionate and authorised recovery, safe degraded-mode, practical alternative or planned-transition response appropriate to that obligation.

Observed service state, access and recovery evidence demonstrates that the required level of availability or usable continuity actually held, or that applicable and justified limits were handled through a sufficient response; publication of a nominal fallback alone is not enough.

exclusions: Class scope exclusion (all results): An outage, ordinary service variation, transient inconvenience, dissatisfaction or adverse outcome without an independently evidenced and applicable availability, usable-quality or continuity requirement.

Class scope exclusion (all results): One inaccurate or harmful AI output without evidence of a service-level availability or governed functional-degradation defect; assess applicable output or decision-integrity classes.

For failure-occurrence admission: a lawful and proportionate safety, security, abuse-prevention, service-maintenance or other valid restriction that is consistent with the applicable service obligation and feasible alternative or transition measures. This exclusion does not defeat a successful-invariant mapping supported by all success recognition conditions.

For failure-occurrence admission: a temporary incident with an effective and proportionate degraded or recovery route that satisfies the applicable requirement, or an unavoidable disruption for which no relevant feasible response was required. This exclusion does not defeat a successful-invariant mapping supported by all success recognition conditions.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The only demonstrated error is an incorrect description of access or outage state while the functional service obligation remains satisfied; assess FC-032.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The only demonstrated defect is loss of otherwise-valid access because a dependent identity or licence verification cannot complete; assess FC-048 unless an independent broader service availability requirement also failed.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The only demonstrated defect is loss of durable work state or inaccurate restored work state while service-function availability requirements are otherwise satisfied; assess FC-035 or FC-036.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The only demonstrated defect is infrastructure access coercion or compelled governance concessions; assess FC-058 or FC-059 as appropriate.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The only demonstrated defect is failure to provide an interaction-level protection response to evidenced vulnerability; assess FC-087, allowing co-occurrence only for a separately evidenced service-level continuity failure.
